messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - Dedicated pool 'dedicated-blueoak-1' GPU capacity exhausted for tenant 'Blue Oak' - autoscale/burst failed. Paging oncall.

luis-oncall: I'm on it. Pulling metrics now. Can someone drop the pool config?

chandra-sre: seeing a sharp spike in active token/sec for that tenant starting ~00:10 UTC. Their sessions are holding long KV caches. Could be a runaway batcher + long-context jobs.

samir-ops: confirmed. Pool utilization 100% (8/8 GPUs). All requests for route `blueoak-prod/*` pinned to this pool. No burst allowed — policy says reserved for enterprise.

maria-customer-success: pinging account-rep and Acme contact. Account rep says Acme is running nightly data-gen job they didn't notify us about. they're trying to finish a large inference sweep.

joel-eng: Links: dashboard -> https://console.redwood/internal/pools/dedicated-blueoak-1/utilization
Logs snippet: ```
2026-03-15T00:12:03Z request_id=abc123 tenant=blueoak route=chat model=gpt-small quant=fp16 latency=120ms
2026-03-15T00:12:04Z queue.waits=0.9s batch.size=32
2026-03-15T00:12:04Z gpu=0 util=100% mem=98% kv_cache=large
```

luis-oncall: options brainstorm: 1) permit immediate burst into shared pool (risking noisy neighbor), 2) manually add 2 GPUs to dedicated pool (if capacity in region), 3) route some blueoak traffic to hosted fallback model (rate/quality tradeoff), 4) request customer to throttle/stop job.

chandra-sre: manual add requires on-call infra runbook approval and nodetypes available. I can try API to allocate if infra has spare. Running: `redwood-admin pools allocate --pool-id=dedicated-blueoak-1 --gpus=2` to check.

samir-ops: runbook snippet (for reference): ```bash
# try burst into shared
redwood-admin pools update --pool-id=dedicated-blueoak-1 --allow-burst=true --burst-threshold=0.8
# or allocate
redwood-admin pools allocate --pool-id=dedicated-blueoak-1 --gpus=2 --type=ondemand
```

account-rep: customer has not pre-approved burst into shared. they requested isolation for compliance. must get explicit ok. I've started a call with their infra lead.

maria-customer-success: On call now with Blue Oak (PM + infra). They can pause the sweep but it will take 15-30m to stop. They asked if we can provide a temporary degraded path for non-critical requests.

luis-oncall: Ok. Immediate mitigation plan: A) Route non-critical endpoints to hosted fallback model `redwood/gpt-xx-small` with quantization to reduce GPU footprint. B) Throttle or drop batch size for long-context sweep requests via routing policy. C) If customer approves, enable burst to shared for 30m. Which do we do now?

joel-eng: I can push a quick routing change: set route `blueoak-prod/embeddings` -> fallback-hosted for requests with header `x-priority: low`. Here's the rule: ```json
{
  "match": "route == 'blueoak-prod/embeddings' && header.x-priority == 'low'",
  "action": "redirect",
  "target": "hosted/gpt-128-quant"
}
```

chandra-sre: deploying that rule now to canary (1 worker) then will promote. Pushing: `redwood-config apply --file canary-rule.json --env=prod`

samir-ops: while that's rolling, I can try to allocate 2 GPUs as ondemand. chandra, do we have spare capacity in us-east-1?

chandra-sre: quick check: `redwood-admin infra list-nodes --region=us-east-1 --available=true` -> 1 node with 4 GPUs available. Should be enough to add 2. I'm going to run allocate now but it will take ~3-5 minutes to schedule and warm the runtime.

acme-support-bot: BlueOak (customer) message: "We're pausing the sweep — hitting stop now. ETA 20m. Thanks for the heads up."

luis-oncall: Good. Let's proceed with routing change + allocation as safety. Prioritize canary so we don't flip everything. Also set a guard: if error rate increases we rollback.

joel-eng: Canary applied. Monitoring latencies. So far low-priority traffic diverted. GPU queue for dedicated pool dropped from 100% -> 85% in last 90s.

samir-ops: Allocation command returned success; new nodes scheduled. Pool size now 10 GPUs (8->10). Warmup complete, sched delay cleared. Utilization 72% after shift.

luis-oncall: Confirming customer impact: CS said no user-facing degradations reported, only internal batch job. Marking impacted services: `blueoak-prod` internal sweep only. Severity remains P1 until fully stable.

account-rep: Customer asked for cost estimate for the extra 2 GPUs for the 40m window. I'll calculate and send.

maria-customer-success: I'll follow up with Blue Oak to confirm they saw the pause and ask for formal change control before next big sweep.

chandra-sre: Immediate next steps (short): 1) Keep canary rule for 1h, 2) keep allocated nodes for 1h, 3) schedule postmortem with infra + account team. 4) Update runbook to include automatic notify to account-rep when reserved pool approaches 90% sustained for >5m.

luis-oncall: I'm handing off to chandra for overnight monitoring. If utilization re-spikes to >90% after CS confirms job resumed, escalate to infra paging.

chandra-sre: acknowledged. Taking over oncall. Will update as things change.

samir-ops: for the follow-up postmortem let's capture: why policy didn't block batch size 32 for reserved pool, whether autoscale/burst policy can include a 'soft-burst' that requires account approval but auto-notify account-rep, and add detection for sustained KV-heavy sessions.

maria-customer-success: Blue Oak confirmed they will add a job window to avoid peak hours and will request temporary burst in future in advance. They're appreciative of the quick mitigation. :thumbsup:

luis-oncall: Closing loop: incident resolved for now. I'll leave thread open for postmortem notes. Thanks all. :party-parrot:

chandra-sre: Action items assigned: `ENG-1423` - runbook update, `INFRA-798` - soft-burst feature spec, `CS-445` - customer coordination docs. Scheduling postmortem tomorrow 16:00 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> RESOLVED (mitigated). Root cause: tenant-run batch job exhausted dedicated pool. Temporary mitigations: routing to hosted fallback, manual allocation of 2 GPUs, customer paused job. Next steps: postmortem and runbook updates."
